evidence.quote: We're switching from PostgreSQL to QuantumDB

observations.why: Speaker controls and supplies the decision as established fact, exercising informational power by stating the migration as settled rather than proposing it.
Evidence-and-benefit argument: quantitative performance gain plus cost reduction offered as justification, blending rational persuasion with reward framing.
Arrow notation frames the migration as a settled transition, controlling the factual presentation rather than arguing for it.
Quantified performance claim presented as evidence to support the decision — classic rational-persuasion tactic.
Fixed deadline attached to the migration creates temporal pressure, anchoring the decision to a specific quarter.

mints.name: DecisionAsFactStated
mints.title: We're switching
mints.frame: Is the speaker asserting a decision as already settled rather than proposing or consulting — and does that framing itself carry the power move?
